headline: DeepSeek: 600 billion dollars lost in a day
text: DeepSeek, a Chinese AI start-up, released an advanced AI model that it says it developed at a fraction of the usual cost and computing power, and its app overtook ChatGPT as the top free app in the US App Store. On 27 January Nvidia's shares fell so sharply that it lost about 600 billion dollars of market value, the largest one-day loss for any US company.
imageCaption: Jensen Huang at the CES keynote, Las Vegas, 6 January 2025

headline: Stargate and the DeepSeek shock
text: On 21 January OpenAI, Oracle and SoftBank announced Stargate, a plan to spend up to 500 billion dollars on AI data centres in the US over four years. A week later DeepSeek, a Chinese AI model released on 20 January, topped the US App Store; on 27 January Nvidia fell 17%, losing about 600 billion dollars of value, the largest one-day loss for any US company.
imageCaption: President Trump with SoftBank's Masayoshi Son, Oracle's Larry Ellison and OpenAI's Sam Altman announcing the Stargate investment, White House, 21 January 2025

headline: GE Aerospace orders jump 46%
text: On 23 January GE Aerospace reported fourth-quarter orders up 46% to 15.5 billion dollars, revenue up 14%, and operating profit up 49%. It expects another year of substantial growth in 2025.
imageCaption: GE Aviation's engine maintenance works at Nantgarw, Wales

headline: Software growth and an AI order book lift IBM
text: IBM's fourth-quarter software revenue grew 10%, led by Red Hat, and its book of generative AI business passed 5 billion dollars. Chief executive Arvind Krishna forecast revenue growth of at least 5% and free cash flow of about 13.5 billion dollars for 2025.
imageCaption: IBM's chief executive Arvind Krishna with Japan's prime minister Shigeru Ishiba and officials, Tokyo

headline: Musk's politics hit Tesla's sales and shares
text: In February, Musk's first full month leading the Department of Government Efficiency, which is cutting the federal workforce, Tesla shares fell 28%, their worst month since December 2022. Protesters gathered at Tesla showrooms, Tesla's sales in the EU and UK nearly halved in January, and its German sales fell 76% in February. Fourth-quarter car revenue had fallen 8%.
source: CNBC, 'Tesla's worst month since 2022 coincided with Elon Musk's first full month in White House', 4 March 2025, https://www.cnbc.com/2025/03/04/elon-musk-first-month-in-white-house-was-tesla-worst-month-since-2022.html (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. (protests, European sales, read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Elon Musk at the Conservative Political Action Conference, 21 February 2025

headline: Freixe's first results lift the share
text: On 13 February Nestlé reported 2024 organic growth of 2.2% and a trading margin of 17.2%. Freixe promised a CHF 2.5 billion cost-saving programme over three years and more spending on advertising, and said growth should improve in 2025 while the margin stays at or above 16%.
imageCaption: Laurent Freixe, chief executive of Nestlé, at the World Economic Forum

headline: Tariffs of 145% on China
text: On 2 April President Trump announced tariffs on most of the world, 34% on China. After China retaliated, the US raised its tariff on Chinese goods to 104% and then 145%; China replied with 125%. Trade between the two biggest economies is close to a halt.
imageCaption: Container terminal at Yangshan, the port of Shanghai

headline: Liberation Day: tariffs crash shares, a pause brings a record rebound
text: On 2 April President Trump announced tariffs of at least 10% on nearly all imports. The S&P 500 fell 4.8% on 3 April and 6.0% on 4 April, the largest two-day loss of value in history at about 6.6 trillion dollars, and on 7 April it was briefly 23% below its February record. On 9 April Trump paused most of the tariffs and the index jumped 9.5%, its biggest daily gain since 2008; it ended April down only 1%.
imageCaption: President Trump announces reciprocal tariffs in the White House Rose Garden, 2 April 2025

headline: Liberation Day: tariffs on the whole world
text: On 2 April President Trump announced tariffs on imports from almost every country: 10 percent for all from 5 April, and higher 'reciprocal' rates from 9 April, including 20 percent for the EU, 34 percent for China and 31 percent for Switzerland. Stock markets crashed for two days. On 9 April Trump paused the higher rates for 90 days, and the S&P 500 had its biggest one-day gain since 2008. The Swiss rate was met with incomprehension in Bern.
imageCaption: President Trump shows his chart of 'reciprocal' tariffs in the White House Rose Garden, 2 April 2025

headline: Export licence required for China chips: a 5.5 billion dollar charge
text: On 9 April the US government told Nvidia that it needs a licence to export its H20 chips, designed for the Chinese market, to China, and on 14 April that this applies indefinitely. Nvidia expects charges of up to about 5.5 billion dollars for H20 inventory and purchase commitments.
imageCaption: Nvidia's headquarters in Santa Clara, California

headline: Tariffs knock oil below $60
text: After the US announced sweeping tariffs on 2 April, fears of a recession hit oil: US crude fell from $72 to about $60 by 8 April, the lowest since 2021, and ended the month 17% lower at $59.55. OPEC+ is in the process of unwinding its output cuts.
imageCaption: An oil tanker in the North Sea

headline: Tariff shock: Treasury bonds sold, gold bought
text: After the president announced sweeping tariffs on 2 April, the S&P 500 fell 10 percent in two days. Treasury bonds, the usual safe haven, were sold too: the 10-year yield rose from 3.86 percent on 4 April to 4.5 percent on 9 April, and the 30-year yield jumped 54 basis points to 4.92 percent, its biggest three-day rise since 1982, before a 90-day tariff pause on 9 April calmed markets. Gold averaged 3,218 dollars in April, 8 percent more than in March and a record.
imageCaption: The reciprocal tariff rates announced at the White House, 2 April 2025

headline: Buffett, 94, announces he will step down as chief executive
text: At Berkshire's annual meeting on 3 May Warren Buffett said he would ask the board to make Greg Abel, vice chairman for the non-insurance businesses, chief executive at the end of the year. On 4 May the board voted unanimously to appoint Abel president and chief executive from 1 January 2026; Buffett remains chairman.
imageCaption: Warren Buffett

headline: Disney beats forecasts and raises its outlook
text: On 7 May Disney reported quarterly revenue up 7% to 23.6 billion dollars and adjusted earnings up 20% to 1.45 dollars a share. Disney+ added 1.4 million subscribers instead of losing them, US parks profit rose 13%, and Disney raised its full-year earnings forecast to 5.75 dollars a share.
imageCaption: Cinderella Castle, Magic Kingdom, Walt Disney World ;;

headline: Twelve days of war: Israel and the US strike Iran
text: On 13 June Israel launched surprise strikes across Iran, killing senior military commanders and nuclear scientists and hitting nuclear and missile sites; Iran answered with hundreds of ballistic missiles and drones fired at Israeli cities. On 22 June US bombers struck the nuclear sites at Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan, and Iran fired missiles at a US base in Qatar. A ceasefire took hold on 24 June. Hundreds were killed in Iran, many of them civilians, and dozens in Israel.
imageCaption: Smoke over Tehran after the Israeli attack of 13 June 2025

headline: Israel and Iran at war for twelve days
text: Israel struck Iran's nuclear and military sites on 13 June; the US bombed three nuclear sites on 22 June, and a ceasefire took hold on 24 June. Brent rose from about $68 to over $78, then fell back to about $68 once oil kept flowing through the Strait of Hormuz.
imageCaption: Israeli Air Force fighter jets on their way to Iran, June 2025

headline: Bern wants UBS to hold much more capital
text: In June the Swiss Federal Council proposed tougher rules for systemically important banks, drawing lessons from Credit Suisse: among other things, investments in foreign subsidiaries would have to be fully backed by top-quality capital. On 6 June UBS estimated it would need about $24 billion of additional common equity in its parent bank if the rules were adopted as proposed. Parliament still has to decide.
imageCaption: Karin Keller-Sutter, the Swiss finance minister

headline: Azure passes 75 billion dollars a year
text: On 30 July Microsoft reported revenue of 76.4 billion dollars for the quarter to June, up 18%, and net income of 27.2 billion. Azure, its cloud business, passed 75 billion dollars in revenue for the year, up 34%, and Nadella called cloud and AI the driving force of business transformation.
imageCaption: Microsoft's headquarters campus in Redmond, Washington

headline: The first four-trillion-dollar company
text: On 10 July Nvidia became the first company ever to close with a market value above four trillion dollars, worth more than all listed companies in the United Kingdom together.
imageCaption: Jensen Huang at the White House AI Summit, Washington, 23 July 2025

headline: The US government takes 10% of Intel
text: Lip-Bu Tan, a veteran chip investor, has been chief executive since March. On 18 August SoftBank agreed to invest 2 billion dollars in Intel. On 22 August President Trump announced that the government will convert grants promised to Intel under the CHIPS Act into shares: it buys 433.3 million shares at 20.47 dollars, 8.9 billion dollars for about 10% of the company.
imageCaption: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick with Intel chief executive Lip-Bu Tan, August 2025

headline: Trump hits Switzerland with a 39 percent tariff
text: On Swiss National Day, 1 August, Washington announced a 39 percent tariff on Swiss goods from 7 August, the highest in Europe and far above the 15 percent agreed with the EU, saying Switzerland refused to make significant concessions. Federal President Karin Keller-Sutter said the Federal Council was disappointed and that the rate was far higher than the one negotiated; the machinery industry fears for tens of thousands of jobs. Pharmaceuticals remain exempt for now.
imageCaption: Karin Keller-Sutter, President of the Swiss Confederation

headline: Nvidia invests 5 billion dollars in Intel
text: On 18 September Nvidia agreed to buy 5 billion dollars of Intel shares at 23.28 dollars, about 4% of the company, and the two will develop chips together for PCs and data centres. Intel's shares closed 22.8% higher at 30.57 dollars, their best day since 1987.
imageCaption: Jensen Huang, Nvidia's chief executive, at the CES keynote, Las Vegas, January 2025

headline: Chief executive fired; chairman leaves early
text: On 1 September Nestlé dismissed chief executive Laurent Freixe with immediate effect and without severance, after an investigation found an undisclosed romantic relationship with an employee. Philipp Navratil, a Zurich-born Nestlé veteran who has run Nespresso since 2024, replaces him. Chairman Paul Bulcke said he would leave at the end of September, six months earlier than planned.
imageCaption: Philipp Navratil, who takes over as chief executive of Nestlé

headline: Nvidia invests in Intel and in OpenAI
text: On 18 September Nvidia agreed to invest 5 billion dollars in Intel, about 4% of its old rival, and to develop chips with it. On 22 September Nvidia and OpenAI signed a memorandum under which Nvidia would invest up to 100 billion dollars in OpenAI, which would use Nvidia systems for data centres of at least 10 gigawatts.
imageCaption: UK prime minister Keir Starmer and Jensen Huang on stage at an Nvidia event, 2025

headline: Musk buys a billion dollars of Tesla shares
text: Elon Musk bought about 1 billion dollars of Tesla shares, adding to his roughly 13% stake, in what investors took as a vote of confidence; the shares jumped more than 6% on 15 September. Musk wants more control of Tesla as he pushes it into robotaxis, automation and artificial intelligence.
source: BBC, 'Musk buys $1bn worth of Tesla shares', 15 September 2025, https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cp982z3xrz7o (read 2026-10-03); CBS News, 'Tesla's stock surges after CEO Elon Musk buys $1 billion worth of shares', 15 September 2025 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Elon Musk, chief executive of Tesla

headline: Nvidia invests $1 billion in Nokia
text: On 23 October Nokia reported third-quarter sales up 9% on a comparable basis, with optical networks up 19%. On 28 October Nvidia announced it will invest 1 billion dollars in Nokia at 6.01 dollars a share and work with it on AI-powered mobile networks for 5G-Advanced and 6G, with T-Mobile US trials from 2026.
imageCaption: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang (centre) at Stanford University

headline: Takaichi takes over; Nikkei passes 50,000
text: Sanae Takaichi won the leadership of the Liberal Democratic Party on 4 October and became Japan's first woman prime minister on 21 October. The Nikkei jumped 4.75% past 47,000 after her win and passed 50,000 on 27 October, on hopes of more government spending.
imageCaption: Sanae Takaichi at a press conference after her election as prime minister, 21 October 2025

headline: Citigroup agrees to sell a quarter of Banamex
text: Citigroup reported third-quarter net income of $3.8 billion, up from $3.2 billion, and said it has agreed to sell a 25% stake in its Mexican bank Banamex, a step toward selling it entirely; it took a $726 million goodwill charge on the deal. It returned $12 billion to shareholders in the first nine months. The shares are around $100, the highest since the autumn of 2008.
imageCaption: A former Banco Nacional de Mexico (Banamex) building, now a shop

headline: Five trillion dollars
text: On 29 October Nvidia became the first company to reach a market value of five trillion dollars.
imageCaption: Nvidia's GTC conference entrance, 2025

headline: Gold passes 4,000 dollars
text: Gold rose above 4,000 dollars an ounce for the first time in October and averaged 4,058 dollars, 11 percent more than in September. The Fed resumed cutting on 17 September and cut again on 29 October, to 3.75 to 4 percent, though inflation is still about 3 percent.
imageCaption: 400-ounce gold bars

headline: Nvidia at 5 trillion; a stake in Nokia
text: On 29 October Nvidia became the first company valued at 5 trillion dollars. In October it agreed a partnership with Nokia on AI in mobile networks and took a stake in the Finnish company, whose shares rose 44% in October. JPMorgan's chief Jamie Dimon warned of a higher chance of a meaningful drop in stocks.
imageCaption: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang delivers the keynote at CES, Las Vegas, January 2025

headline: Siemens outlines a spin-off of its Healthineers stake
text: In November Siemens outlined a plan to hand its majority stake in Siemens Healthineers directly to its own shareholders. Siemens sold part of the stake in February, keeping 73%, and completed the purchase of the engineering software maker Altair for about 10 billion dollars, its largest deal, in March.
imageCaption: A Siemens SPECT/CT scanner in a hospital

headline: McMillon to retire; Walmart moves to Nasdaq
text: On 14 November Walmart said chief executive Doug McMillon will retire at the end of January and be succeeded on 1 February by John Furner, head of Walmart U.S., who joined as an hourly worker in 1993. On 20 November it announced it will move its share listing from the New York Stock Exchange to Nasdaq in December, the largest such switch on record.
imageCaption: Doug McMillon

headline: Cisco's share price passes its 2000 high
text: In December Cisco's shares closed above $80.06, the closing high of March 2000, for the first time in more than 25 years. Investors are buying it as a supplier of networking for AI data centres, including switches developed with Nvidia. Because Cisco has bought back many shares, its market value is still far below the 2000 peak.
imageCaption: Cisco's headquarters, Building 10, San Jose

headline: A copper plan: one million tonnes by 2028
text: At its capital markets day on 3 December Glencore said its copper production should exceed 1 million tonnes a year by the end of 2028 and reach about 1.6 million by 2035, including a restart of the Alumbrera mine in Argentina; it has paid out $25.3bn to shareholders over five years. Copper averaged a record $11,785 a tonne in December.
source: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/glencore--glen/glencore-capital-markets-day-2025-/9273460; World Bank Pink Sheet monthly averages (both read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: The Collahuasi copper mine, Chile

headline: Henrique Braun to succeed James Quincey
text: On 10 December Coca-Cola elected its chief operating officer Henrique Braun, 57, a Brazilian-American who joined the company in 1996, as chief executive from 31 March 2026. James Quincey, CEO for nine years, becomes executive chairman. Under Quincey the company added more than ten billion-dollar brands.
imageCaption: James Quincey, Coca-Cola chief executive

headline: 2025 in review: a third double-digit year in a row
text: The S&P 500 gained 16% in 2025 to 6,845.50, the Nasdaq 19% and the Dow 13%, a third year in a row of double-digit gains. The April tariff crash became an afterthought, and resilient earnings, three Federal Reserve rate cuts from September and enthusiasm for artificial intelligence carried shares to records despite a long government shutdown and worries about an AI bubble.
imageCaption: Nvidia's headquarters in Santa Clara, California

headline: Buying growth: Avidity for $12 billion
text: This year Novartis agreed to buy Avidity Biosciences for about $12 billion, after Anthos Therapeutics ($925 million) and, last year, MorphoSys (EUR 2.7 billion). In the third quarter its sales rose 8% and operating income 24%.
imageCaption: The Novartis campus in Basel
